Advocate Hon'ble Shri Justice P. Sam Koshy Order On Board 20/01/2023
1.

This is the first bail application filed u/s 439 of Cr.P.C. for grant of regular bail to the applicant
who is in jail since 14.02.2022 in connection with Crime No.96/2019 registered at Police Station -
Dantewada, District Dantewada (Cg) for the offence punishable under Sections 420, 34 of Ipc,
Section 4, 5, 6 of the Prize Chits & Money Circulation Schemes (Banning) Act, 1978 and Section 10
of Cg Protection of Depositors Interest Act.

entities.text: Cg Protection of Depositors Interest Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 2. Learned counsel for applicant submits that though in the present crime the applicant stands arrested on 14.02.2022 but in fact the applicant is in continuous custody for a period of almost 7  years as she has been inflicted in many other cases of identical nature.
He submits that in most of the cases the applicant has been released on bail either by the Trial Court or in many of them by the High Court itself.
He further submits that taking into consideration the over all period of custody undergone and the fact that the applicant is a lady, she may be released on bail.

3. State counsel, on the other hand, opposing the bail application submits that the nature of allegations are such where the applicant has defrauded a large number of villagers and that in the instant case the arrest of applicant has been shown only w.e.f. 14.02.2022.
Therefore, it cannot be said that the applicant in the present case has remained in custody for long.

State counsel further submits that the applicant was implicated in the said case on account of the fact that she was the Director of the company namely M/s Sai Prasad Chit Fund Co. though counsel for applicant submits that the applicant had resigned from the Post of Director long back.

sentences.text: Given the entire facts and circumstances of the case and also taking into consideration the fact that firstly the applicant being a lady, secondly she is in continuous custody for a period of almost 7  years and further taking into consideration the fact that this High Court itself in a large number of cases has already granted bail to the applicant, prima facie, a strong case for allowing the present MCRC is made out.
5. Accordingly, the application for grant of bail is allowed.

It is directed that the present Applicant shall be released on bail on her furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- with two sureties in the like sum to the satisfaction of concerned trial Court on the conditions that;
a) she shall appear before the trial Court concerned regularly on each & every date unless exempted from appearance.
b) She shall not, in any manner, tamper with the prosecution witnesses.
c) If applicant is found involved in similar offence in future, it will be open for the State to apply for cancellation of bail.
